name: Gear-Lib
listed_description: A collection of basic libraries in POSIX C for embedded and network service development.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README (raw.githubusercontent.com) is a feature list of 39 libraries (libdict, libhash, libringbuffer, libgevent, libworkq, liblog, libfile and others) with no benchmark, speed or comparison wording; the gear-lib/gear-lib directory listing has no bench, perf or test directories; the repo page shows no benchmark mention (3.2k stars, MIT). One WebSearch for gear-lib benchmarks against libevent and the other likely baselines returned only unrelated libevent and libev pages. Lead gave no claim words.

name: gprof
listed_description: Performance analysis tool. Part of GNU binutils.
reason: gprof is the listed baseline itself, and the only reachable numeric statements run the other way. The GNU binutils manual host sourceware.org is not resolvable (ENOTFOUND) and the GitHub mirror paths tried (bminor/binutils-gdb gprof/gprof.texi) returned 404 or 403, so the gprof manual could not be read. One WebSearch returned only snippets: an ACM paper (doi 10.1145/1088149.1088161, not opened) claiming its sampling-based call-path profiler has over an order of magnitude lower overhead than instrumentation profilers such as gprof, and Red Hat blog posts on perf versus gprofng (a different tool, not opened). No page was found where gprof beats a named baseline with numbers; a gprof-faster-than-callgrind style overhead comparison was not found.

name: HPX
listed_description: A general purpose C++ runtime system for parallel and distributed applications of any scale.
reason: No reachable page with numbers where HPX beats a named baseline. Opened: README.rst (no figures, only 'hundreds of millions of threads' and scalability goals), docs/joss_paper/paper.md (no benchmark numbers), tests/performance/local (benchmark sources such as openmp_homogeneous_timed_task_spawn.cpp, openmp_parallel_region.cpp, stream.cpp, future_overhead.cpp but no stored results), PR 3183 (no numbers), issue 3137 (HPX start/stop 50 ms, HPX suspend/resume 500 us vs OpenMP parallel-for enter/exit 100 us on a dual-socket 18-core Xeon: OpenMP faster), the weilewei/parSTL repo (HPX, Kokkos, GNU, TBB parallel transform and sort harness, no results) and a gist on HPX benchmark standardisation (one hpx::min timing, no baseline). Search snippet only: tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks lists HPX about 161x slower than the best runtime (mean ratio) on a fork-join benchmark, and a June 2026 arXiv preprint 2606.11937 (Strack, Van Craen, Pfluger, tiled Cholesky with OpenMP and HPX, Cholesky-Bench, 128-core AMD Zen 2 node) reports HPX task overhead about 2 us vs about 7.6 us for GCC OpenMP, HPX 15-30% faster at the optimal tile size and async HPX tasks up to 26% faster than their OpenMP analogs; arxiv.org, ar5iv, alphaxiv, emergentmind and puma.ub.uni-stuttgart.de are not resolvable here and a guessed code repo (SC-SGS/Cholesky-Bench) returned 404, so those numbers could not be verified. Worth retrying with paper access: the Cholesky-Bench preprint (HPX vs GCC/LLVM OpenMP) and the Task Bench overheads paper (Wu et al., Charm++ and HPX vs MPI/OpenMP, seen only in a snippet). The HPX repo also appears under TheHPXProject/hpx.

name: imtui
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README (raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com page, 3.6k stars, MIT, last commit 2025-10-10) has demos and build notes only; imtui is a Dear ImGui port that draws through ncurses, so ncurses is a dependency rather than a baseline; the repo listing (examples, include, src, third-party, CHANGELOG.md) has no benchmark content and no frame-rate or overhead claim. One WebSearch for imtui versus ncurses or termbox performance found no benchmark.
